```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(Lahman)
library(rvest)
library(tidyverse)
head(HallOfFame)
str(HallOfFame)
View(HallOfFame)
```

## R Markdown

```{r}
library(rvest)

url <- "https://www.baseball-reference.com/awards/hof_2026.shtml"
page <- read_html(url)

tables <- html_table(page, fill = TRUE)
length(tables)
head(tables[[1]])
head(tables[[2]])
```

Filer 2026 Data 
```{r}
hof_2026 <- subset(HallOfFame, yearID == 2026)
head(hof_2026)
```

```{r}
url <- "https://www.baseball-reference.com/awards/hof_2026.shtml"
page <- read_html(url)

tables <- html_table(page, fill = TRUE)

length(tables)
head(tables[[1]])
```

```{r}
data <- tables[[1]]
actual_col_names <- data[1, ]
colnames(data) <- actual_col_names
data <- data[-1, ]
data<-data|> select(Name, Votes,`%vote`) |> mutate(Year=2026,Inducted=ifelse(parse_number(`%vote`)>=75, 'Yes','No'))
head(data, 3)
```

```{r}
write.csv(data, file="hall of fame_ 2026-file.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
